---
title: "Project structure and wiring"
---

`uvx capt-hook init` already wired your project, scaffolding `.claude/hooks/`, the skills, and the `settings.local.json` that points Claude Code at them.

## What `init` creates

```
your-project/
├── .claude/
│   ├── hooks/
│   │   └── example.py           # the starter hook
│   ├── skills/                  # bootstrapping-hooks + translating-styleguides
│   └── settings.local.json      # the wiring (below)
```

Hooks are just Python files under `.claude/hooks/`. An optional `conf.py` beside them holds
[settings](../guide/configuration.qmd). `init` doesn't create it; add one when you need it.
`uvx capt-hook test` and `uvx capt-hook run` both default `--hooks` to that directory; pass
`--hooks <dir>` to point elsewhere.

## The wiring contract

`init` writes the `hooks` block of `.claude/settings.local.json`, and `register-hooks`
regenerates it. Each event maps to the one command Claude Code runs:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "uvx capt-hook run PreToolUse" } ] }
    ],
    "Stop": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "uvx capt-hook run Stop" } ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

Only the events your hooks listen on appear. `uvx capt-hook run <Event>` is the one
place the `uvx` convention is baked into a file instead of typed by you.

## How a hook runs

When an event fires, Claude Code runs `uvx capt-hook run <Event>` and talks to it over a pipe:

1. Claude Code writes the event as JSON to the process's **stdin**:

   ```json
   {"tool_name": "Bash", "tool_input": {"command": "git stash"}}
   ```

2. captain-hook loads every hook in `.claude/hooks/`, runs the ones that match, and writes the
   verdict to **stdout**:

   ```json
   {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PreToolUse",
     "permissionDecision": "deny", "permissionDecisionReason": "..."}}
   ```

3. Claude Code reads the verdict. `deny` blocks the tool, `allow` lets it through, and an
   advisory hook injects `additionalContext` instead.

## When to re-wire

Editing a hook's body needs nothing. The same `uvx capt-hook run` command picks it up. Re-run
`register-hooks` when you add a hook on a **new event**, or your first async hook on an
already-wired one, so the event gets its own entry:

```bash
uvx capt-hook register-hooks           # writes settings.local.json
uvx capt-hook register-hooks --dry-run # print the merged JSON without writing
```

Then reload the project so Claude Code reads the updated settings. `.claude/hooks/` is code, so
commit it, and review hook changes in pull requests like anything else.

The wired event set is derived from your registered hooks, not a fixed list, so a hook on an event
no entry covers never fires. captain-hook catches this. On the next synchronous event it warns the
agent through `additionalContext` to re-run `uvx capt-hook register-hooks`, so a forgotten re-wire
surfaces instead of silently swallowing the hook.
